Which government department decided that owners cannot return to Wang Fuk Court?

Multiple owners raised the issue during the Q&A session. At least five speakers questioned Hap On about which department made the decision to bar residents from returning to Wang Fuk Court and what legal basis underpinned the lockdown. Hap On initially dodged the question four times, merely saying that Wang Fuk Court had not yet been unsealed and that the matter fell outside the manager's authority to arrange, and advised owners in need to contact their dedicated social worker — a response that drew jeers from owners at several venues.

Hap On does not know the legal basis on which the authorities imposed the lockdown

Solicitor Leung Ping-chiu finally responded that Hap On did not know the legal basis on which the authorities imposed the lockdown and it would be inappropriate for him to explain on their behalf for fear of misrepresenting the government's considerations. As for the inspection reports for the other seven blocks of Wang Fuk Court, which also drew much attention, Hap On said that with the typhoon and rainy seasons approaching, the reports might be released once the authorities had completed their inspections. It also said that after taking legal advice, Hap On considered that the demand exceeded its responsibilities as manager.

Owners concerned the government will use donations to reclaim titles — will skipping rebuilding save China Taiping compensation?

The government has previously stated that it will not rebuild on the original site. At the meeting, several owners asked whether this meant the HK$2 billion "fire insurance" payout, calculated on the cost of restoring the building's structure, would not be honoured. "Will the government use the donations to reclaim the titles and not rebuild, so as to save China Taiping the compensation?" A representative from China Taiping Insurance (Hong Kong), Ms Lau, said that once policy liability was established, the company would pay out in accordance with the policy terms regardless of whether repairs or rebuilding took place, and that any acquisition would not affect policy liability or the amount calculated. However, Ms Lau also said that the specific policy and legal liability could only be further assessed after the independent committee and various government departments had completed their investigations and announced the results.

Indicating repairs to Wang Chi House would cost HK$30 million

Hap On also reported on the situation at Wang Chi House, which was unaffected by the fire. Hap On had previously said that repairing Wang Chi House would cost at least HK$30 million and take at least nine months, involving re-tiling the external walls, restoring the electrical system and more; today it updated the total to about HK$32 million and the works period to between three and nine months. Solicitor Leung Ping-chiu, invited by Hap On to attend the meeting, pointed out that Wang Chi House formed part of the entire estate under the Deed of Mutual Covenant, and separating it out would require substantial amendments to the DMC with the consent of all owners — a complicated and costly procedure.

Some owners questioned why Hap On, citing the time needed to contact owners as a reason for not convening an owners' meeting within the statutory deadline, had nevertheless managed to issue funding cheques on behalf of the Urban Renewal Authority earlier this year, asking, "I'd like to know what's so difficult — you can't find us owners for a meeting?" Hap On Property Services Director Chan Wai-kwong, who chaired the meeting, did not answer directly, saying it was a venue issue and that finding a space capable of holding a thousand residents was genuinely difficult; ultimately, it was only after the Home Affairs Department provided a venue that the meeting could be held. Some owners criticised the explanation as unreasonable: "Hong Kong hosts so many of those mega events and spectacle-economy shows drawing tens of thousands to a single venue — and you're telling me you can't find a place for our 2,000 people? That's really hard to swallow. I hope you won't use this as an excuse again."
